Thinking about getting a face and neck lift and weighing options in Northern California vs. Seoul, given the massive price difference. Any recommendations?
9
Most relevant﻿
Katarzyna Jonas
 
·
1w
 
·
Follow
I can understand why Seoul is tempting with such a big price difference. Have you started getting consultations in either location yet?
Reply
Share
GivingNectarine8993
 
·
1w
Katarzyna Jonas I’d compare more than just the surgery fee. Travel, accommodation, medication and follow-up appointments can add quite a bit to the total.
Reply
Share
Katarzyna Jonas
 
·
1w
 
·
Follow
That's what I'd be concerned about with going overseas. What happens if you have an issue once you're back home?
Reply
Share
GivingNectarine8993
 
·
1w
Exactly. I'd want a clear aftercare plan and to know who to contact if complications or unexpected swelling occur after returning.
Reply
Share
Katarzyna Jonas
 
·
1w
 
·
Follow
I'd also check the surgeon's specific experience with both face and neck lifts, rather than relying only on clinic reviews.
Reply
Share
GivingNectarine8993
 
·
1w
Same here. Before-and-after photos of patients with similar facial structure and concerns would be helpful too.
Reply
Share
Katarzyna Jonas
 
·
1w
 
·
Follow
Do you know whether the consultations in Seoul are directly with the surgeon who would perform the operation?
Reply
Share
Francisco Alves de Oliveira
 
·
1w
The price difference is real, but compare the full cost and the risks, not just the surgeon's fee. Seoul has very experienced facial surgeons. Northern California makes follow-up and handling complications much simpler. When I compared going abroad for one of my own procedures, the travel, the extra days and the aftercare plan changed the numbers more than I expected.
If you're considering Seoul:
1. Check that the surgeon is board-certified by the Korean Society of Plastic and Reconstructive Surgeons, and confirm that the surgeon you meet is the one who operates. Ask if the surgery can be recorded.
2. Ask for healed results at 1 year or more on patients with faces like yours. Many Korean clinics specialize in Asian anatomy and aesthetics, so if your features are different, make sure they have plenty of experience with them.
3. Plan to stay at least 10 to 14 days, until the stitches are out and the swelling is down enough for a long-haul flight. Ask your surgeon about blood clot prevention for the flight home.
4. Arrange a local surgeon or clinic at home who will see you if anything comes up, since many US surgeons won't take on complications from surgery done abroad.
5. Add up flights, accommodation, someone to travel with you, and extra time off, then compare that total with the California quotes.
For Northern California, use the "Find a Surgeon" tools from the American Society of Plastic Surgeons or the American Academy of Facial Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery, and compare at least two or three consults on both sides before you decide.
When I had my own surgery, my doctor recommended a book called YOU'VE DECIDED ON PLASTIC SURGERY. NOW WHAT?: EVERYTHING YOU NEED TO KNOW ABOUT MAKING THE RIGHT DECISIONS, PREPARING YOUR BODY, AND RECOVERING WITH CONFIDENCE by Marcus Michael. It goes through how to compare surgeons at home and abroad and what to ask before booking. The book is on Amazon Kindle.
Reply
Share
Daisy Chambers
That NorCal vs Seoul gap for a face and neck lift had me going in circles too — on paper Seoul wins on price, but what settled it for me was how differently the two consults looked at my neck: one surgeon spent most of the time on the neck laxity, the other barely checked past the jawline. How young is too young to have surgery? One side of my face is heavy/bloated looking compared to the other. I dont know the best option for me but so insecure
2
5
Most relevant﻿
Dr Carl's Truesdales, M.D.
 
·
21w
 
·
Follow
Age alone isn't the deciding factor—it's your anatomy, concerns, and goals. Facial asymmetry is very common, and one side appearing heavier doesn't always require surgery. The best first step is a consultation with a board-certified facial plastic surgeon to determine the cause and discuss whether non-surgical treatments or surgery would be most appropriate. A personalized evaluation is always the safest approach
Reply
Share
GreenMango4476
 
·
21w
Dr Carl's Truesdales, M.D. how long does a face-lift usually last?
Reply
Share
Beachme01
 
·
21w
Maybe surgery is not the answer . Fully address your overall health
Reply
Share
GreenMango4476
 
·
21w
SundaySwimgal_ my health is overall good
Reply
Share
Daisy Chambers
I asked myself the exact same 'too young' question — one side of my face always looked heavier in photos too, and it made me feel self-conscious for years. What finally helped me was a consult where the surgeon looked at the asymmetry itself instead of my age, because the fix depends on what's actually causing the heaviness. Is it mostly the heaviness on one side that bothers you, or the worry that you're too young for surgery at all?

How often does a facelift need to be redone? If I were to get one in my early 40’s about how long would it last? TIA!
4
26
1
Most relevant﻿
Lisa Haws
 
·
18w
This is an interesting question because you will always have a new set point. You will always look better than you would have had you not gotten a FL. Now will you want more done later? Possibly. Does it completely fall apart? No
Reply
Share
Zara Bennett
 
·
18w
My doctor said if I go back yearly for C02 fractional laser and fat transfer under my eyes that it will last me 20 to 30 years I’m 49.
Reply
Share
Edited
Theresa Webster Kennedy
 
·
18w
By reviewing 30 years of patient data, researchers tracked exactly how long a deep plane facelift preserves its effects before a patient seeks a touch-up. They discovered that patients returned for a revision surgery an average of 11 years (specifically 10.9 years) after their primary procedure. Study out June 2026
Reply
Share
Kate Kvinge Burch
 
·
18w
Just to give you a different perspective, my mom had hers done 40 years ago. Of course she's aged but she looks lovely for an 85 year old. I'd share her picture but she'd get mad at me. Even if you have it done, you're still going to see the effects years later and it will be worth it
Reply
Share
View 1 reply
RelaxingChestnut6169
 
·
18w
Depends on many many factors… when you go through menopause, consistent weight management, and your unique skin, sun protection and skin care! There is no guarantee or definite number of years a lift will last. Another major factor is the type. A deep plan typically lasts longer
Than a SMAS.
Reply

·
18w
10 - 15 years
Reply

AmbitiousHeron1755
 
·
18w
The real answer to this has to do with you. Does your weight fluctuate often ? Do you eat healthy and exercise. Are you constantly in the sun, do you smoke, get good sleep and do you use daily sunscreen? As for the correct timing to get face and neck lift is when you've lost weight (if over weight) and are able to maintain it after the surgery. After all the above is addressed, a true deep plane face and necklift should last you 10 to 15 years.
